questions.prompt: At what smallest positive \(x\) does \(y=-\cos(3 x) + 2\) attain its maximum value?
questions.explanation: The maximum needs \(\cos(3x)=-1\) (because \(b<0\)). The smallest positive angle with that value is \(\pi\), so \(x=\dfrac{\pi}{3}=\frac{\pi}{3}\).

questions.prompt: Find the range of \(y=\dfrac{1}{-4 - 3\sin(3 x)}\).
questions.explanation: Denominator: \(a=-4\), \(|b|=3\), so it runs from \(m=-7\) to \(M=-1\). Both have the same sign, so the denominator never reaches 0 and the reciprocal runs from \(\dfrac1M\) to \(\dfrac1m\): \([-1.0,\ -0.142857142857143]\).

questions.prompt: Find the maximum \(M\) and minimum \(m\) of \(y=\frac{2}{3}\cos(x) + 2\).
questions.explanation: For \(y=a+b\,\cos(\cdots)\) the maximum is \(a+|b|\) and the minimum is \(a-|b|\). Here \(a=2\), \(|b|=\frac{2}{3}\), so \(M=\frac{8}{3}\) and \(m=\frac{4}{3}\). (The sign of \(b\) and the inside of the bracket do not change the extreme values.)

questions.prompt: Find the range of \(y=\dfrac{1}{\frac{3}{2} - 3\sin(2 x - 2)}\).
questions.explanation: The denominator runs from \(m=- \frac{3}{2}\) to \(M=\frac{9}{2}\) and passes through \(0\) (so these \(x\) are excluded from the domain). Then \(y\) takes values \(\le\dfrac1m=- \frac{2}{3}\) or \(\ge\dfrac1M=\frac{2}{9}\), with a gap between. There is no maximum and no minimum.

questions.prompt: How many complete cycles of \(y=\cot(\frac{x}{2})\) appear in the interval \([0,\ 6 \pi]\)?
questions.explanation: Number of cycles \(=\dfrac{\text{length of interval}}{\text{period}}\). The period of \(y=\cot(\frac{x}{2})\) is \(2 \pi\), so in \([0,6 \pi]\) there are \(\dfrac{6 \pi}{2 \pi}=3\) complete cycles.

questions.prompt: Find the period of \(f(x)=\frac{1}{2}\tan(\frac{3 \pi x}{2} - 3)\).
questions.explanation: The period of \(\tan(bx+c)\) is \(\dfrac{\pi}{|b|}\) (tan and cot repeat every \(\pi\), not \(2\pi\)). Here \(b=\frac{3 \pi}{2}\), so the period is \(\frac{2}{3}\).

questions.prompt: Find the period of \(f(x)=3\sin(3 x)\).
questions.explanation: For \(y=\sin(bx+c)\) the period is \(\dfrac{2 \pi}{|b|}\). Here \(b=3\), so the period is \(\frac{2 \pi}{3}\). The coefficient in front and the shift inside do not change the period.

questions.prompt: A quantity oscillates sinusoidally between a minimum of \(-10\) and a maximum of \(10\) with period \(60\). At \(t=0\) the quantity is at its minimum. Which equation models it?
questions.explanation: Starting at a minimum means \(-\cos\). \(A=10\), midline \(D=0\), \(B=\dfrac{2\pi}{60}=\frac{\pi}{30}\).

questions.prompt: Convert \(\frac{3 \pi}{2}\) radians to degrees.
questions.explanation: Multiply by \(\dfrac{180}{\pi}\): \(\frac{3 \pi}{2}\cdot\dfrac{180^\circ}{\pi}=270^\circ\).

questions.explanation: For \(y=\sin(bx+c)\) the period is \(\dfrac{2 \pi}{|b|}\). Here \(b=\frac{1}{3}\), so the period is \(6 \pi\). The coefficient in front and the shift inside do not change the period.

questions.prompt: A mass on a spring moves according to \(x=6\cos(10t)\) cm, \(t\) in seconds. Find the amplitude of the motion (in cm).
questions.explanation: The amplitude is the coefficient of the cosine: \(6\) cm.

questions.prompt: Find the domain of \(y=\tan(6 x)\).
questions.explanation: \(\tan\theta\) is undefined when \(\cos\theta=0\), i.e. \(\theta=(2n+1)\frac{\pi}{2}\). With \(\theta=6x\): \(x=\dfrac{(2n+1)\pi}{2\cdot6}\).

questions.prompt: An alternating voltage is \(V=110\sin(36000t)^\circ\) volts, where \(t\) is in seconds. Find \(V\) at \(t=\frac{1}{400}\) s.
questions.explanation: The angle is \(36000\times\frac{1}{400}=90^\circ\). So \(V=110\sin90^\circ=110\) V.

questions.prompt: Find the domain of \(y=\operatorname{cosec}(5 x)\).
questions.explanation: \(\operatorname{cosec}\theta\) is undefined when \(\sin\theta=0\), i.e. \(\theta=n\pi\). With \(\theta=5x\): \(x=\dfrac{n\pi}{5}\).

questions.prompt: A Ferris wheel of radius \(40\) m has its lowest point \(1\) m above the ground and makes one revolution in \(72\) s. A rider boards at the lowest point. How high above the ground is the rider after \(18\) s?
questions.explanation: A rider who starts at the lowest point follows \(h(t)=41-40\cos\!\left(\dfrac{2\pi t}{72}\right)\) (centre height \(=\text{radius}+\text{platform}=40+1=41\) m). At \(t=18\) s the angle is \(2\pi\cdot\frac{1}{4}\), \(\cos=0\), so \(h=41\) m.

questions.prompt: At what smallest positive \(x\) does \(y=-3\sin(2 x) + 2\) attain its maximum value?
questions.explanation: The maximum needs \(\sin(2x)=-1\) (because \(b<0\)). The smallest positive angle with that value is \(\frac{3 \pi}{2}\), so \(x=\dfrac{\frac{3 \pi}{2}}{2}=\frac{3 \pi}{4}\).

questions.prompt: State the amplitude of \(y=\frac{3}{2}\sin\left(\frac{3}{2}\left(x-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\right) + 2\).
questions.explanation: Amplitude \(=|a|=\frac{3}{2}\).

questions.prompt: Find the maximum value of \(y=-3\cos^2x + 5\sin^2x\).
questions.explanation: Use \(\sin^2x+\cos^2x=1\): the expression is a weighted average of \(-3\) and \(5\) with weights between \(0\) and \(1\), so it lies between them. Maximum \(=5\), minimum \(=-3\).

questions.prompt: Convert \(\frac{\pi}{6}\) radians to degrees.
questions.explanation: Multiply by \(\dfrac{180}{\pi}\): \(\frac{\pi}{6}\cdot\dfrac{180^\circ}{\pi}=30^\circ\).

questions.prompt: What can be said about the extreme values of \(y=\dfrac{1}{5 + 7\sin(2 x)}\)?
questions.explanation: Denominator from \(-2\) to \(12\): it changes sign (\(|a|<|b|\)) and so passes through 0, where \(y\) blows up. There is no maximum or minimum.

options: It has a maximum but no minimum
It has a minimum but no maximum
It has a maximum and a minimum
It has no maximum and no minimum

questions.prompt: Find the minimum value of \(y=2\sin^2x - 1\cos^2x\).
questions.explanation: Use \(\sin^2x+\cos^2x=1\): the expression is a weighted average of \(2\) and \(-1\) with weights between \(0\) and \(1\), so it lies between them. Maximum \(=2\), minimum \(=-1\).

questions.prompt: A quantity oscillates sinusoidally between a minimum of \(-4\) and a maximum of \(16\) with period \(10\). The model is \(y=D+A\sin(Bt)\) type with \(B>0\). Find \(B\) (radians).
questions.explanation: \(B=\dfrac{2\pi}{T}=\dfrac{2\pi}{10}=\frac{\pi}{5}\).

questions.prompt: Is \(f(x)=x^3 \cdot \cos x\) even, odd, or neither?
questions.explanation: Parities of the factors: \(x^3\) is odd, \(\cos x\) is even. There are 1 odd factor (a product or quotient is odd exactly when the number of odd factors is odd), so the function is odd.

questions.prompt: Find the domain of \(y=\sec(x)\).
questions.explanation: \(\sec\theta\) is undefined when \(\cos\theta=0\), i.e. \(\theta=(2n+1)\frac{\pi}{2}\). With \(\theta=1x\): \(x=\dfrac{(2n+1)\pi}{2\cdot1}\).

questions.prompt: Find the range of \(y=\dfrac{1}{1 - 5\cos(2 x)}\).
questions.explanation: The denominator runs from \(m=-4\) to \(M=6\) and passes through \(0\) (so these \(x\) are excluded from the domain). Then \(y\) takes values \(\le\dfrac1m=-0.25\) or \(\ge\dfrac1M=0.166666666666667\), with a gap between. There is no maximum and no minimum.

questions.prompt: In the model \(h=D-R\cos(Bt)\), what does \(D\) represent?
questions.explanation: \(D\) is the midline, the height of the hub.

options: The height of the wheel's centre above the ground

questions.prompt: Find the range of \(y=\dfrac{1}{\frac{3}{2} + \frac{5}{2}\sin(x + 1)}\).
questions.explanation: The denominator runs from \(m=-1\) to \(M=4\) and passes through \(0\) (so these \(x\) are excluded from the domain). Then \(y\) takes values \(\le\dfrac1m=-1\) or \(\ge\dfrac1M=\frac{1}{4}\), with a gap between. There is no maximum and no minimum.

questions.prompt: Find the range of \(y=\dfrac{1}{-2 - 4\sin(2 x + 1)}\).
questions.explanation: The denominator runs from \(m=-6\) to \(M=2\) and passes through \(0\) (so these \(x\) are excluded from the domain). Then \(y\) takes values \(\le\dfrac1m=-0.166666666666667\) or \(\ge\dfrac1M=0.5\), with a gap between. There is no maximum and no minimum.

questions.prompt: Find the period of \(f(x)=\sin(\frac{5 x}{2}) + \cos(6 x)\).
questions.explanation: First find the two periods: \(\frac{4 \pi}{5}\) and \(\frac{\pi}{3}\). The period of a sum is \(\dfrac{\text{LCM of numerators}}{\text{HCF of denominators}}\). Writing the periods as fractions of \(\pi\): \(\frac{4}{5}\) and \(\frac{1}{3}\) give \(4\pi\). So the period is \(4 \pi\).

questions.prompt: Find the period of \(f(x)=2\sin(5 x)\).
questions.explanation: For \(y=\sin(bx+c)\) the period is \(\dfrac{2 \pi}{|b|}\). Here \(b=5\), so the period is \(\frac{2 \pi}{5}\). The coefficient in front and the shift inside do not change the period.

questions.prompt: Find the maximum \(M\) and minimum \(m\) of \(y=-6\cos(x) + 5\).
questions.explanation: For \(y=a+b\,\cos(\cdots)\) the maximum is \(a+|b|\) and the minimum is \(a-|b|\). Here \(a=5\), \(|b|=6\), so \(M=11\) and \(m=-1\). (The sign of \(b\) and the inside of the bracket do not change the extreme values.)

questions.prompt: Find the period of \(f(x)=\cot(2 x) + \tan(6 x)\).
questions.explanation: First find the two periods: \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) and \(\frac{\pi}{6}\). The period of a sum is \(\dfrac{\text{LCM of numerators}}{\text{HCF of denominators}}\). Writing the periods as fractions of \(\pi\): \(\frac{1}{2}\) and \(\frac{1}{6}\) give \(\frac{1}{2}\pi\). So the period is \(\frac{\pi}{2}\).

questions.prompt: Find the maximum \(M\) and minimum \(m\) of \(y=5\sin(x) - 1\).
questions.explanation: For \(y=a+b\,\sin(\cdots)\) the maximum is \(a+|b|\) and the minimum is \(a-|b|\). Here \(a=-1\), \(|b|=5\), so \(M=4\) and \(m=-6\). (The sign of \(b\) and the inside of the bracket do not change the extreme values.)

questions.prompt: Find the period of \(f(x)=6\tan(\frac{3 x}{5} + 5)\).
questions.explanation: The period of \(\tan(bx+c)\) is \(\dfrac{\pi}{|b|}\) (tan and cot repeat every \(\pi\), not \(2\pi\)). Here \(b=\frac{3}{5}\), so the period is \(\frac{5 \pi}{3}\).

questions.prompt: A mass on a spring moves according to \(x=10\cos(5t)\) cm, \(t\) in seconds. How far is the mass from the centre of the motion at \(t=0\) (in cm)?
questions.explanation: \(x(0)=10\cos0=10\) cm: it starts at maximum displacement.

questions.prompt: The height of a buoy above the sea bed is modelled by \(d(t)=10+4\cos\!\left(\dfrac{2\pi t}{6}\right)\), \(t\) in hours. How many hours pass between two successive maxima?
questions.explanation: The time between successive maxima is one period \(=\dfrac{2\pi}{2\pi/6}=6\) hours.

questions.prompt: An alternating voltage is \(V=100\sin(14400t)^\circ\) volts, where \(t\) is in seconds. Find \(V\) at \(t=\frac{1}{60}\) s.
questions.explanation: The angle is \(14400\times\frac{1}{60}=240^\circ\). So \(V=100\sin240^\circ=- 50 \sqrt{3}\) V.

questions.prompt: A mass on a spring moves according to \(x=6\cos(2t)\) cm, \(t\) in seconds. How far is the mass from the centre of the motion at \(t=0\) (in cm)?
questions.explanation: \(x(0)=6\cos0=6\) cm: it starts at maximum displacement.

questions.prompt: Find the range of \(y=\dfrac{1}{-5 + \cos(x)}\).
questions.explanation: Denominator: \(a=-5\), \(|b|=1\), so it runs from \(m=-6\) to \(M=-4\). Both have the same sign, so the denominator never reaches 0 and the reciprocal runs from \(\dfrac1M\) to \(\dfrac1m\): \([-0.25,\ -0.166666666666667]\).

questions.prompt: An alternating voltage is \(V=170\sin(18000t)^\circ\) volts, where \(t\) is in seconds. Find \(V\) at \(t=\frac{1}{120}\) s.
questions.explanation: The angle is \(18000\times\frac{1}{120}=150^\circ\). So \(V=170\sin150^\circ=85\) V.

questions.prompt: State the amplitude of \(y=\sin\left(\frac{1}{2}x\right) - 2\).
questions.explanation: Amplitude \(=|a|=1\).

questions.prompt: Find the domain of \(y=-2\tan(\frac{2 x}{3})\).
questions.explanation: \(\tan\theta\) is undefined when \(\cos\theta=0\), i.e. \(\theta=(2n+1)\frac{\pi}{2}\). With \(\theta=\frac{2}{3}x\): \(x=\dfrac{(2n+1)\pi}{2\cdot\frac{2}{3}}\).

questions.prompt: A Ferris wheel has radius \(20\) m, its lowest point is \(5\) m above the ground and one revolution takes \(30\) s. In the model \(h=D-R\cos(Bt)\), find \(B\) (in radians per second).
questions.explanation: \(B=\dfrac{2\pi}{T}=\dfrac{2\pi}{30}=\frac{\pi}{15}\).

questions.prompt: State the frequency (number of cycles per unit of \(x\)) of \(y=4\cos\left(\frac{1}{2}\left(x+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\right) + 4\).
questions.explanation: Frequency \(=\dfrac1T=\dfrac{|b|}{2\pi}=\frac{1}{4 \pi}\).

questions.prompt: Is \(f(x)=\dfrac{\tan x}{x^2}\operatorname{cosec}x\) even, odd, or neither?
questions.explanation: Parities of the factors: \(\tan x\) is odd, \(x^2\) is even, \(\operatorname{cosec}x\) is odd. There are 2 odd factors (a product or quotient is odd exactly when the number of odd factors is odd), so the function is even.

questions.prompt: Find the range of \(y=5\sin(4 x - 1) + 1\).
questions.explanation: \(-1\le\sin(\cdots)\le1\), so multiplying by \(5\) gives \([-5,5]\) and adding \(1\) shifts it to \([-4,\ 6]\). The inside part only changes the period.

questions.prompt: Find the range of \(y=\dfrac{1}{6 - 3\sin(\frac{x}{2} + 1)}\).
questions.explanation: Denominator: \(a=6\), \(|b|=3\), so it runs from \(m=3\) to \(M=9\). Both have the same sign, so the denominator never reaches 0 and the reciprocal runs from \(\dfrac1M\) to \(\dfrac1m\): \([0.111111111111111,\ 0.333333333333333]\).

questions.prompt: If \(\cos\theta=- \frac{5}{13}\) and \(\theta\) is in the second quadrant, find \(\sec\theta\).
questions.explanation: Use \(\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1\) to find the missing ratio, then fix its sign from the quadrant (ASTC). Here \(\sin\theta=\frac{12}{13}\), \(\cos\theta=- \frac{5}{13}\), so \(\sec\theta=- \frac{13}{5}\).

questions.prompt: Find the minimum value of \(y=2\sin(2 x + 3) - 4\).
questions.explanation: For \(y=a+b\,\sin(\cdots)\) the maximum is \(a+|b|\) and the minimum is \(a-|b|\). Here \(a=-4\), \(|b|=2\), so \(M=-2\) and \(m=-6\). (The sign of \(b\) and the inside of the bracket do not change the extreme values.)

questions.prompt: The depth of water in a harbour is modelled by \(d(t)=6+\cos\!\left(\dfrac{2\pi t}{8}\right)\), \(t\) in hours. Find the difference between the greatest and least values.
questions.explanation: Difference \(=2A=2\).

questions.prompt: The function \(f(x)=\cot(kx)\) (\(k>0\)) has period \(\frac{\pi}{3}\). Find \(k\).
questions.explanation: The period of \(\cot(kx)\) is \(\dfrac{\pi}{k}\). Setting \(\dfrac{\pi}{k}=\frac{\pi}{3}\) gives \(k=3\).

questions.prompt: A Ferris wheel of radius \(20\) m has its lowest point \(1\) m above the ground and makes one revolution in \(36\) s. A rider boards at the lowest point. How high above the ground is the rider after \(30\) s?
questions.explanation: A rider who starts at the lowest point follows \(h(t)=21-20\cos\!\left(\dfrac{2\pi t}{36}\right)\) (centre height \(=\text{radius}+\text{platform}=20+1=21\) m). At \(t=30\) s the angle is \(2\pi\cdot\frac{5}{6}\), \(\cos=\frac{1}{2}\), so \(h=11\) m.

questions.prompt: Find the period of \(f(x)=3\cos(\frac{5 x}{2})\).
questions.explanation: For \(y=\cos(bx+c)\) the period is \(\dfrac{2 \pi}{|b|}\). Here \(b=\frac{5}{2}\), so the period is \(\frac{4 \pi}{5}\). The coefficient in front and the shift inside do not change the period.

questions.prompt: A quantity oscillates sinusoidally between a minimum of \(13\) and a maximum of \(21\) with period \(60\). The model is \(y=D+A\sin(Bt)\) type with \(B>0\). Find \(B\) (radians).
questions.explanation: \(B=\dfrac{2\pi}{T}=\dfrac{2\pi}{60}=\frac{\pi}{30}\).

questions.prompt: Find the range of \(y=7\sin(\frac{2 \pi x}{3} + 4)\).
questions.explanation: \(-1\le\sin(\cdots)\le1\), so multiplying by \(7\) gives \([-7,7]\). The inside part only changes the period.

questions.prompt: Find the period of \(f(x)=\sin^{3}(6 x)\).
questions.explanation: An odd power of sin or cos keeps its sign changes, so the period stays \(\dfrac{2\pi}{|b|}\). Here \(b=6\), so the period is \(\frac{\pi}{3}\).

questions.prompt: How many times does the graph of \(y=\sin(6 x)\) cross the \(x\)-axis for \(0<x\le\pi\)?
questions.explanation: The zeros of \(y=\sin(6 x)\) are at \(x=\dfrac{n\pi}{6}\). Counting those with \(0<x\le\pi\) gives 6.

questions.prompt: Find the period of \(f(x)=\cot(\frac{x}{4}) + \sin(\frac{7 x}{3})\).
questions.explanation: First find the two periods: \(4 \pi\) and \(\frac{6 \pi}{7}\). The period of a sum is \(\dfrac{\text{LCM of numerators}}{\text{HCF of denominators}}\). Writing the periods as fractions of \(\pi\): \(4\) and \(\frac{6}{7}\) give \(12\pi\). So the period is \(12 \pi\).

questions.prompt: Find the period of \(f(x)=\left|\sin(\frac{3 x}{2})\right|\).
questions.explanation: Taking the absolute value folds the negative half of the wave upwards, so the pattern repeats after half a period: \(\dfrac{\pi}{|b|}\). Here \(b=\frac{3}{2}\), so the period is \(\frac{2 \pi}{3}\).

questions.prompt: Find the exact value of \(\cos\,105^\circ\).
questions.explanation: Write \(105^\circ\) as a sum or difference of special angles (e.g. \(45^\circ\pm30^\circ\) or \(60^\circ\pm45^\circ\)) and use the compound-angle formulas. The result is \(- \sqrt{\frac{1}{2} - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}}\).
